title: Perf canary: gate merges on tiered SLO regressions (p95/p99) for top models/regions
creator: Sofia Ivanova
description:
Context
- We’re shipping workload-aware batching defaults with 3 customer-facing latency SLO tiers (fast / standard / cost-efficient).
- To avoid silent tail-latency regressions during scheduler/knob iteration, we need perf-canary to block merges when tier-specific SLO metrics regress beyond agreed thresholds for a curated set of top model families + regions.

Goal
- Add tier-aware gating to perf-canary so that merges are blocked on statistically meaningful regressions relative to baseline, aligned with the tier SLO definition doc and benchmark methodology.
- Primary focus: fast-tier p99 protections and standard-tier p95 stability (cost-efficient tier is allowed to trade latency for throughput, but we still need a guardrail against pathological queue blowups).

Non-goals (for this ticket)
- Not implementing the runtime knobs or tier selection logic (covered by ENG-18422/23/24/25).
- Not designing new benchmark scenarios (covered by ENG-18427 + benchmark-lab changes).
- Not building dashboards/alerts (covered by ENG-18429).

Proposed gating policy (v1)
1) Scope: only top model families and “high-signal” regions
- Models (initial): Llama-family 8B/70B class, Mistral-family, Qwen-family (exact identifiers pulled from benchmark-lab config).
- Regions (initial): us-east-1, us-west-2, eu-west-1.
- Hardware classes: use the canonical perf-canary hardware pool(s) already used for runtime PR gating; don’t expand fleet in v1.

2) Metrics and thresholds
- Fast tier
  - Gate on p99 end-to-end latency regression (prefill+decode) for both streaming and non-streaming scenarios.
  - Default threshold: fail if p99 regresses by > X% OR > Y ms (absolute cap), whichever is smaller.
  - Rationale: fast tier is the “realtime” expectation; tail latency is the foot-gun we must catch.
- Standard tier
  - Gate on p95 end-to-end latency regression.
  - Default threshold: fail if p95 regresses by > X% OR > Y ms.
  - Rationale: standard tier should remain stable for most customers; p95 is the best proxy for broad experience while reducing noise vs p99.
- Cost-efficient tier
  - Guardrail gate: fail only on “blowup” patterns (queue depth explosion correlated with latency) OR p95 regression beyond a larger bound.
  - Rationale: cost-efficient is allowed to be slower; we mainly want to prevent scheduler pathologies under mixed workloads.

3) Baseline handling
- Use moving baseline with an explicit refresh process (requires approval) to avoid “baseline drift” hiding regressions.
- Baseline refresh should include:
  - annotated reason (expected improvement / scenario changed / noise reduction)
  - links to PR(s) that motivated refresh
  - confirmation that SLO doc thresholds remain unchanged

4) Regression decision rule / noise control
- Require N repeated runs for failing scenario before hard-fail (N tuned based on current canary variance; start with N=2 for p99-gates, N=1 for p95-gates if variance is low).
- When failing, output:
  - scenario id (model, region, tier, streaming flag, workload mix)
  - baseline value, current value, delta
  - link to raw run artifacts
  - (if available) tier profile selection reason codes present during run

Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Perf-canary config supports “tier” as a first-class dimension (fast/standard/cost-efficient) and runs tier-specific scenarios from benchmark-lab.
- [ ] Gating rules implemented for fast-p99 and standard-p95 at minimum, with explicit thresholds committed in config (not ad-hoc).
- [ ] Cost-efficient guardrail gate implemented (either relaxed p95 bound or blowup detection using queue/latency correlation if available in artifacts).
- [ ] Failure output is actionable (clear diff vs baseline, scenario identifiers, links).
- [ ] Documented baseline refresh process + ownership (SRE sign-off required).
- [ ] Dry-run mode supported for 1 week (report-only) before enforcing hard merge blocks.

Implementation plan (current)
1) Update benchmark-lab scenario naming and output schema
- Consume tier-specific scenario ids from benchmark-lab PR (expected: mixed workload tier scenarios).
- Ensure we can unambiguously map a run to: tier + streaming + model + region.

2) Add tier-aware gates to perf-canary
- Implement gate definitions in perf-canary repo config:
  - fast: p99, streaming+non-streaming
  - standard: p95, streaming+non-streaming
  - cost-efficient: relaxed bounds or blowup detection
- Add human-readable error messages and links.

3) Rollout
- Phase 0: report-only in perf-canary (no blocking) for ~1 week.
- Phase 1: enforce on runtime scheduler PRs only (label-based), then expand to runtime repo default branch protection.

Open questions
- What are final numeric X% / Y ms per tier? Waiting on final SLO tier numeric targets (ENG-18421) + observed variance from mixed workload scenarios.
- Should we gate on TTFT separately for streaming fast tier? (fast-tier p99 is the current priority; TTFT may come later if signal is strong.)
- Which model list qualifies as “top models” for gating vs “informational only” runs?

Links / references
- Linear deps: ENG-18421 (tier SLO targets), ENG-18427 (mixed workloads), ENG-18426 (reason codes)
- Related PRs (expected):
  - perf-canary: pr-489-gate-on-fast-tier-p99-and-standard-tier-p95
  - benchmark-lab: pr-612-add-mixed-workload-slo-tier-scenarios
- Confluence references:
  - Latency SLO tiers definition (fast/standard/cost-efficient)
  - Batching SLO tier benchmark methodology

Updates
- 2026-02-12 (Sahana): Drafted initial gating spec (fast p99, standard p95). Biggest risk is p99 variance; proposing 2-run confirmation before hard fail.
- 2026-02-18 (Sean Gallagher): SRE wants baseline refresh to require explicit approval + audit trail (no silent refresh). Add “report-only week” before enforcing.
- 2026-02-21 (Marcus Reed): Mixed workload scenarios in benchmark-lab are close; scenario ids may change once promptset weighting is finalized. Suggest we code against stable tier labels + streaming flag, not hardcoded scenario names.
- 2026-02-27 (Rafael Mendes): For rollout, start enforcement only on PRs touching scheduler codepaths (path filter) to reduce early friction; expand once we’re confident in variance and thresholds.

Requested reviewers
- Marcus Reed (scheduler/perf suite)
- Rafael Mendes (reliability gates, rollout)
- Sean Gallagher (SRE sign-off on enforcement + baseline refresh)
- Allison Grant (observability/metrics sanity; ensure we can debug failures quickly)

Notes
- This ticket is intentionally conservative in v1: gate the most customer-visible regressions (fast tail latency) while controlling CI flakiness. We can tighten thresholds and expand model/region scope after we have a few weeks of stable signal.
